drhp.business: Amagi provides a unified, cloud-based platform that integrates production, preparation, distribution and monetization workflows for the streaming video value chain (glass-to-glass, camera-to-screen). It serves three customer categories - content providers, distributors and advertisers - across three business divisions (Cloud Modernization, Streaming Unification, and Monetization & Marketplace). As of September 30, 2025 it served over 400 content providers, over 350 distributors and over 75 advertisers across more than 40 countries.
drhp.end_markets: Content providers (TV networks, movie studios, production companies, sports leagues)|Distributors (OTT platforms, telecom operators, smart-TV manufacturers)|Advertising platforms and advertisers (demand-side platforms, ad agencies, brands)
drhp.expansion: Amagi is a SaaS business with no manufacturing plants; its expansion narrative is investment in technology and cloud infrastructure plus international customer expansion and inorganic acquisitions, rather than physical capacity.

market_position.basis: The DRHP states: 'Our Company is a cloud-native SaaS provider offering end-to-end solutions across live production, content preparation, distribution, and monetization in the broadcasting and streaming ecosystem. There are no listed players in India or abroad in the broadcasting and streaming ecosystem.' No peer P/E comparison is given; P/E is not ascertainable because FY25 EPS is negative. Positioned as a differentiated, cloud-native, glass-to-glass platform in a market where most competitors offer point solutions on legacy architectures. Serviceable addressable market estimated at ~US$5.1 billion (as of Dec 31, 2024).

industry_peers.no_peer_note: The DRHP states under 'Industry Peer Group P/E ratio': 'Our Company is a cloud-native SaaS provider offering end-to-end solutions across live production, content preparation, distribution, and monetization in the broadcasting and streaming ecosystem. There are no listed players in India or abroad in the broadcasting and streaming ecosystem.' Consequently the P/E ratio is shown as NA and the DRHP notes that since Basic and Diluted EPS for FY ended March 31, 2025 is negative, the P/E ratio of the Company is not ascertainable.

genesis.founding_story: Incorporated at Bengaluru, Karnataka as 'Amagi Technologies Private Limited' under the Companies Act, 1956 (CoI dated February 1, 2008). Founded by Baskar Subramanian, Srividhya Srinivasan and Arunachalam Srinivasan Karapattu, who each subscribed 15,000 equity shares on incorporation. The company built a cloud-native platform for the streaming/broadcast video value chain and scaled internationally through multiple venture-capital rounds (Accel, Norwest, PI Opportunities, General Atlantic, etc.).

concerns_observed: History of losses and negative cash flows: restated losses of Rs 3,212.68 million (FY23), Rs 2,450.01 million (FY24) and Rs 687.14 million (FY25); operating cash flow was negative Rs 2,005.95 million in H1 FY26 even after a positive Rs 335.74 million in FY25.

Heavy dependence on a single cloud provider (AWS): a Rs 24,176.20 million (USD 272.50 million) six-year spend commitment (May 2025-April 2031); technology & cloud infrastructure cost was 26.07% of total expenses in FY25.
Revenue concentration by geography: America 72.86% and Europe/UK 17.34% of FY25 revenue; India only ~1.4% - exposing results to US/European macro and trade-policy (tariff) risk.
Foreign-currency exposure without active hedging (~99% of revenue is export).

Low promoter alignment: the three founder-promoters hold only 13.99% (fully diluted) pre-Offer; the entire Offer for Sale of 26,942,343 shares is by investor/individual selling shareholders, and promoter average cost of acquisition is ~Rs 0.88-0.89 per share.

Up to 25% of gross proceeds is earmarked for inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions (no defined target), and the deployment of Net Proceeds has not been appraised by any bank/financial institution.

Statutory-audit modification: auditors were unable to comment on the audit-trail feature for parts of the period and noted the prior-year audit trail was not preserved per record-retention requirements.
Employee- and share-based-cost intensity: employee benefits expense was 53-58% of total expenses; total share-based payments expense was Rs 1,060.10 million (FY25).
data_gaps: The routed 'financials' text carried only the accounting-ratio table (EPS/RoNW/NAV/EBITDA) plus MD&A/Risk-Factor expense tables; the full restated balance sheet, cash-flow statement, working-capital days, debt profile and receivables ageing were not present.
Offer price band, total Net Proceeds, post-Offer promoter holding and dilution percentage are stated as [bullet] in the DRHP.
Top-1/5/10 customer revenue-concentration percentages are not disclosed as a table.
The DRHP industry label mapped to UNMAPPED in the sector spine (no industry alias added, per finish-batch no-code-edit constraint).
No listed-peer benchmarking (P/E, RoNW, NAV) is available - the DRHP states there is no comparable listed entity and FY25 EPS is negative.

parameter_scores.basis: Loss-making FY23-FY25 (restated loss Rs 687.14 mn FY25); first restated profit Rs 64.70 mn in H1 FY26; PAT margin 0.88% H1 FY26.
Gross margin 64.73% -> 69.33% (FY23-FY25); opex fell from 85.47% to 67.30% of revenue; Adjusted EBITDA turned positive in FY25.
Operating cash flow negative in FY23 (-Rs 2,452.36 mn), FY24 (-Rs 1,829.90 mn) and H1 FY26 (-Rs 2,005.95 mn); positive only in FY25 (Rs 335.74 mn).
America 72.86% + Europe/UK 17.34% of FY25 revenue; a few key customers material; offset by 400+ content providers and no top-10 churn.
Single dominant cloud provider (AWS) with a Rs 24,176.20 mn six-year commitment; ~26% of expenses.
Independent-majority-influenced board with 2 IDs and 2 investor nominees; but promoter holding only 13.99%, audit-trail modification, and delays in statutory dues/ESOP/CS-appointment filings.
Rs 5,500.64 mn for cloud infrastructure (no asset creation - recorded as expense); up to 25% of gross proceeds for unidentified acquisitions; Net Proceeds not appraised.
P/E not ascertainable (negative FY25 EPS of Rs 3.48); DRHP states no listed peer exists, so no peer P/E/RoNW/NAV benchmark; offer price is book-built ([bullet]).

red_flags: Bonus issue in the ratio 1:35 (33,211,325 shares) on October 9, 2024, shortly before the IPO, alongside promoter average cost of acquisition of ~Rs 0.88-0.89 per share.
Loss-making across FY23-FY25 with negative operating cash flow in H1 FY26; profitability is only one interim period old.
Statutory auditors' modification on the audit-trail feature (not enabled/preserved for parts of the period; prior-year audit trail not preserved per record-retention rules).
Up to 25% of gross proceeds earmarked for unidentified acquisitions with deployment not appraised by any bank/financial institution.
Promoter holding of only 13.99% (fully diluted) pre-Offer, with the entire Offer for Sale by investor/individual selling shareholders.
strengths_observed: High, capital-efficient top-line growth: revenue from operations grew from Rs 6,805.58 million (FY23) to Rs 8,791.55 million (FY24) to Rs 11,626.37 million (FY25) - a 30.70% CAGR - and rose 34.58% to Rs 7,048.23 million in H1 FY26.
Improving unit economics: gross margin expanded from 64.73% (FY23) to 69.33% (FY25); net revenue retention was 126.90% (FY25); operating expenses fell from 85.47% to 67.30% of revenue over FY23-FY25.
Turned to a restated profit in H1 FY26 (Rs 64.70 million) after losses in FY23-FY25, with Adjusted EBITDA positive (Rs 234.86 million FY25; Rs 582.25 million H1 FY26).

Differentiated, cloud-native, glass-to-glass platform in a segment the DRHP states has no listed peer in India or abroad; three-sided marketplace (content providers, distributors, advertisers) with network-effect flywheel.

Global blue-chip customer base (Vevo, Lionsgate, DAZN, Sinclair, VIZIO, Roku, The Trade Desk, JioAds) with 4.0-year average tenure among the ten largest and no observed top-10 churn across FY23-FY25 and H1 FY26.

Award-winning technology with integrated AI (Amagi INTELLIGENCE), 10 granted patents, a 547-strong engineering team (55.48% of headcount), and the first Technology & Engineering Emmy awarded to an Indian company (2024).
